name: shellbags
description: Walk BagMRU in UsrClass.dat or NTUSER.DAT and return the folders a shell opened on this account: the reconstructed path, the key's last-write time (raw FILETIME and ISO), the shell item's own DOS timestamps (local time, to two seconds) and the MRU order. It reaches folders on devices and shares that are long gone; it does not say who opened them. Every BagMRU root the hive has is walked and named (the Shell and ShellNoRoam trees can both be populated) and each entry says which; a numbered value with no key under it is decoded and listed under values_without_subkey, not dropped; values are read whole (regipy's default cut to 128 bytes is not taken). A shell item's long name is read from its layout only for the file entry extension (0xbeef0004) versions 3, 7, 8 and 9, at the offset the libfwsi notes give for the version (0x14, 0x26, 0x2A, 0x2E), bounded by the block's declared size, and only when the block's own name offset (the 2-byte field at 0x10) agrees and what is there is a printable string that ends inside the block (long_name_from: layout, extension_layout: decoded; a localised name after it, where there is one, is localized_name); in any other case the long name is the longest string found in the block, labelled long_name_from: strings with extension_layout saying why the layout was not applied, a candidate and not a decode. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. A key whose subkey list was already walked (a cycle) is a problem, not walked again; a shell item that cannot be decoded is listed as undecodable. Other shell item classes are string candidates (decoded: strings). max_depth is 1 to 128; keys below it are listed under not_walked_below_max_depth, and problems are a page. The tool stops at its own time limit (115 seconds) and names the keys it did not walk (status partial); SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Result files are named from the hive, the roots and whether contains was given, never from the needle, and are never replaced (another needle takes the next free -n name). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a name, are counted and never printed. Every answer carries status and status_basis. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (shell item names, paths and registry keys): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text. A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text that is shown, never to what is withheld. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on 1,000 random plants per shape and context (175 cells): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys, connection strings, user-info (also with an @ inside the password), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, case-folded and glued prefixes: none printed whole; AWS-shaped, 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys: at most 2.2% (letters-only keys with a slash); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters: at most 0.5%; random lower-case letters of 24: 9.4%; a 16-character base32 seed: 11%. Real Windows strings changed (any part withheld) in 9,950 generated registry, file, service, package and host names, SIDs, GUIDs and typed digests (2 changed: the 32-digit hash in a Chrome and an Edge autolaunch value name) and 3,431 strings of real event logs (25 changed: 17 of 1,040 whole event records, 7 of 313 command lines and messages, 1 of 322 path fields; they hold encoded PowerShell payloads and the 32-digit hash directories of the .NET native-image cache). NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits, anything under 16 characters in a name; 75% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

hive.description: An extracted UsrClass.dat (or NTUSER.DAT for the older location)

key.description: Override the BagMRU root when the hive puts it somewhere unusual (then only that root is walked)

contains.description: Keep only paths containing this string, case-insensitive

max_depth.description: How deep to walk (default 24, at most 128); a key below it that has subkeys is named in not_walked_below_max_depth

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole tree is walked, and when more entries match the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
